name: mincore
synopsis: int mincore(void *addr, size_t length, unsigned char *vec);
description: mincore() returns a vector indicating whether pages of the calling process's virtual memory are resident in core, avoiding page faults if referenced. It provides residency information for pages starting at addr for length bytes. The returned information is a snapshot and may be stale immediately.

parameters.name: addr
parameters.description: Starting address of the memory region to query; must be a multiple of the system page size.

parameters.name: length
parameters.description: Length in bytes of the memory region; effectively rounded up to the next multiple of the page size.

parameters.name: vec
parameters.description: Pointer to an array that will store residency information, with at least ((length + PAGE_SIZE - 1) / PAGE_SIZE) bytes.

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: Kernel is temporarily out of resources.
vec points to an invalid address.
addr is not a multiple of the page size.
length is greater than (TASK_SIZE - addr), or the address range contains unmapped memory.

bugs: Before Linux 2.6.21, mincore() did not return correct information for MAP_PRIVATE mappings or nonlinear mappings established using remap_file_pages(2).
